question: Shared: prediction of MCI-to-AD conversion among ADNI MCI participants, with structural MRI as the shared channel. P-199 (Lu et al., Front Aging Neurosci 2022) uses one baseline T1 volume (3D ResNet-50 initialised from Med3D and pretrained with MoCo) for conversion within 3 years, 577 MCI, random 80/20 split. P-211 (Cai et al., Brain Sci 2023) uses an Explainable Boosting Machine on baseline FreeSurfer volumes/thicknesses plus cognitive scores, demographics, baseline EMCI/LMCI diagnosis and APOE4 (Comb. (a)), with separate models for conversion within 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 years, 1042 amnestic MCI, 90/10 split with 5-fold CV. Horizon, added channels, architecture and validation differ, which condition 1 allows.
metric: AUC with AUC (the recorded pair: 0.835 vs 0.92). Both papers also print accuracy.

figures.P-199: Held-out 20% test set: AUC 0.835, no AUC interval printed. Test class sizes from the printed sensitivity 0.786 = 44/56 and specificity 0.850 = 51/60: 56 pMCI / 60 sMCI (116 subjects; 95/116 = 0.819 accuracy). Hanley-McNeil: Q1 = 0.835/1.165 = 0.7167, Q2 = 2(0.835^2)/1.835 = 0.7599, SE = 0.0382, 95% CI [0.760, 0.910]. Accuracy 0.819 with a printed bootstrap 95% CI of 0.798-0.841; that interval is about a third of the width the 116-subject test set allows (binomial SE sqrt(0.819*0.181/116) = 0.036). Wilson on n = 116: centre (0.819 + 1.9208/116)/(1 + 3.8416/116) = 0.809, half-width 0.070, CI [0.739, 0.878].
figures.P-211: Five-year model, Comb. (a): AUC 0.92, accuracy 85% (225 participants at 5 years: 85 dementia / 140 MCI), no interval printed. Hanley-McNeil over the 5-fold CV sample: Q1 = 0.92/1.08 = 0.8519, Q2 = 2(0.92^2)/1.92 = 0.8817, SE = 0.0214, CI [0.878, 0.962]; over a 10% test set (about 9/14): SE 0.0676, CI [0.788, 1.000]. Three-year model on test data: AUC 0.81 with interaction effects (0.78 without), accuracy 0.75, sensitivity 0.78, specificity 0.73; 3-year cohort 188 dementia / 392 MCI (32% converters). Hanley-McNeil for 0.81 at a 10% test set (about 19/39): Q1 = 0.6807, Q2 = 0.7250, SE = 0.0659, CI [0.681, 0.939]; over the whole 3-year cohort: SE 0.0207, CI [0.769, 0.851]. For 0.78 at the test-set n: CI [0.644, 0.916]. Accuracy 0.75, Wilson at about 58 test subjects: CI [0.625, 0.844].

matched_figure_check: A matched figure exists and reconciles the recorded pair. P-211 reports its model at P-199's 3-year horizon on its test data: AUC 0.81 with interaction effects (0.78 without). Both lie inside P-199's interval [0.760, 0.910], and P-199's 0.835 lies inside P-211's 3-year interval under either evaluation-set assumption ([0.681, 0.939] at the test-set n; [0.769, 0.851] over the whole 3-year cohort). The recorded gap is P-211's horizon effect: its AUC reaches a low point at 3 years and rises to about 0.92 at 5 years. The same 3-year model's accuracy (0.75) lies below P-199's printed bootstrap interval (0.798-0.841), which runs opposite to the recorded disagreement; but 0.75 lies inside P-199's subject-count Wilson interval [0.739, 0.878], P-199's 0.819 lies inside P-211's [0.625, 0.844], and the two test sets differ in converter share (32% vs 48%), with near-equal sensitivities (0.78 vs 0.786) and the difference in specificity (0.73 vs 0.85). P-211's MRI-only arm (Comb. (c)) is shown only in Figure 2, without usable numbers.
performance_validity: Exclusion does not apply: 0.835 and 0.92 are below 0.97. Both are internal evaluations in ADNI.
reason: The recorded AUCs (0.835 vs 0.92) are apart beyond uncertainty on the headline figures (0.92 lies above P-199's upper bound 0.910; 0.835 lies below P-211's five-year bound 0.878 over its CV sample), but the pair sets P-211's five-year model against a three-year one. At the matched three-year horizon P-211 prints AUC 0.81, which agrees with P-199's 0.835 in both directions. The papers' own figures therefore dissolve the gap and condition 3 fails, as in C-149 and C-150 for the same P-211 figures. The three-year accuracy (0.75 vs 0.819) crosses only P-199's printed bootstrap interval, which is narrower than its 116-subject test set allows, and runs opposite to the recorded disagreement.

quotes.quote: As deﬁned in this study, participants with MCI at baseline who developed or did not develop AD within 3 years were referred to as pMCI and sMCI, respectively.
ResNet-50 achieved the best performance with an accuracy of 0.819 and an AUC of 0.835
A total of 10,000 bootstrap replicates were extracted from the test set, and the performance metrics of the model on each bootstrap replicate were calculated.
The ﬁve-years prediction accuracy reached 85% (AUC = 0.92) using both cognitive scores and MRI markers.
The dataset is divided into training and test sets with a percentage, respectively, of 90% and 10%.
The AD percentages were 12%, 27%, 32%, 36%, and 38% within 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 years follow up periods, respectively, with an increasing trend.

The mean AUC using Comb (a) displayed a characteristic pattern of ﬁrst at about 0.9, then decreasing, reaching a low point at 3 years, followed by a gradual increase until 5 years of follow-up, to about 0.92.

The main performance indicators, accuracy, sensitivity, speciﬁcity, and AUC, were 0.75, 0.78, 0.73, and 0.81 (with interaction effects) compared to 0.72, 0.76, 0.68, and 0.78 (without interaction effects), respectively.
